name: ASAP4b
description: Bright-optimized ASAP4 variant with superior brightness and photostability for extended two-photon recordings.

spectrum.name: ASAP4b
spectrum.note: One-photon excitation and emission spectra of ASAP3, ASAP4b and ASAP4e measured in HEK293-Kir2.1 cells at 23 °C (Ext. Fig. 3e; Tecan plate reader, excitation scan 300-530 nm at 550-nm emission, emission scan 500-850 nm under 480-nm excitation). The cyan ASAP4b traces were digitized per-pixel at 1-nm resolution and overlay-verified against the figure. REPLACES a previous curve that was a verbatim copy of the FPbase EGFP spectrum (identical to 1e-8 over all 401 excitation and 238 emission points) mis-attributed to this figure. The real in-cell excitation spectrum is DUAL-BANDED: the global maximum is the protonated (dim-state) chromophore band at ~375 nm, because ASAP4b sits mostly in the protonated state at the -70 mV resting potential of Kir2.1 cells (F-70/Fmax = 0.27, Table 1); the anionic band used for imaging is the broad 400-500 nm plateau at ~0.65-0.75 relative amplitude (ASAP4b is imaged through 484/15-nm or 488-nm excitation filters, and two-photon at 938 nm, Ext. Fig. 3f). peakEx is therefore reported as the digitized curve's true maximum (375 nm), not the imaging wavelength - see the plotted curve. For contrast, ASAP3 in the same panel peaks at 488 nm. Emission peaks at 522 nm (digitized), consistent with the FORCE1s preprint's measured ASAP4e emission peak of 518 ± 4 nm (doi:10.64898/2026.04.07.717088, Fig. S1.2A); ASAP4 variants are redder than ASAP3 (~508 nm) because of the T206H mutation.

voltage.name: ASAP4b
voltage.note: Digitized point-by-point from the F-V plot in Fig. 1b (ASAP4b = blue = ASAP4.2 F413G) at every command-voltage step actually applied (-120, -100, -80, -60, -40, -20, 0, +30, +50, +70, +90 and +120 mV; step positions confirmed from the error-bar centres, and the trace overlay-verified against the figure). -70 mV is the holding potential and is set to 0 by the paper's own normalization (no -70 step was applied; the plotted spline crosses zero near -65 mV). The previous curve was mis-read in the mid-range (-60/-40/-20 stored as 6/24/53 vs the figure's 15/34/66), rescaled at +30 mV to the Table 1 value (+180) instead of the plotted +168, and omitted the +120 mV point entirely. The figure's -70 -> +30 step (+168%) matches the independent Lee 2024 measurement (168%, doi:10.1101/2024.06.21.599617 Table S1) and is slightly below the Table 1 headline of 180% (kept in dynamicRangeData). The response keeps rising to ~+246% at +120 mV.

kinetics.note: Amplitude-weighted mean of bi-exponential fit (Supplementary Table 1, ASAP4b at 22 °C, HEK293A voltage clamp). On (depolarization −70→+30 mV): τfast 2.62 ms (19.1%), τslow 21.21 ms → weighted mean 17.66 ms. Off (repolarization +30→−70 mV): τfast 5.69 ms (8.8%), τslow 24.50 ms → weighted mean 22.85 ms. The main text rounds the depolarization fast component to 2.6 ms (19% amplitude) for ASAP4b vs 3.9 ms (14%) for ASAP4e; Table S1 is the source for the full multi-exponential fit used here.

Amplitude-weighted mean of bi-exponential fit (Supplementary Table 1, ASAP4b at 37 °C). On (depolarization): τfast 1.53 ms (12.5%), τslow 6.13 ms → weighted mean 5.56 ms. Off (repolarization): τfast 1.54 ms (6.5%), τslow 7.38 ms → weighted mean 7.00 ms. As expected, brightness-optimized ASAP4b is slower than speed-optimized ASAP4e (4.55/4.71 ms at 37 °C).

dynamicRangeData.note: ΔF100/F0 across the −70 → +30 mV (100-mV) step, voltage clamp in HEK293A cells under 1P widefield excitation.

apWidthData.sample: HEK293A cells, whole-cell voltage clamp, hippocampal-neuron AP command waveform scaled to 2-ms FWHM (−70 → +30 mV)
apWidthData.note: No optical AP width is printed in the paper, so it was DERIVED by digitizing the averaged optical waveform (cyan ASAP4b trace, top row of Ext. Fig. 5a, n = 7 cells): baseline from the flat pre-spike segment, peak from the maximum deflection, FWHM = the span above the half-baseline-to-peak level, calibrated against the panel's 50-ms scale bar and overlay-verified. The optical response is much broader than the 2-ms command because it is dominated by ASAP4b's own kinetics (weighted τon 17.7 ms / τoff 22.9 ms at 22 °C). Peak amplitude of the same digitized trace recovers 18.7% ΔF/F vs the paper's stated 19%, confirming the trace. Same panel: ASAP3 5.4 ms, ASAP4e 9.1 ms, Upward Ace2N-mNeon 3.8 ms.

apWidthData.sample: HEK293A cells, whole-cell voltage clamp, hippocampal-neuron AP command waveform scaled to 4-ms FWHM (−70 → +30 mV)
apWidthData.note: Derived the same way from the bottom (4-ms FWHM) row of Ext. Fig. 5a. Same panel: ASAP3 8.5 ms, ASAP4e 11.2 ms, Upward Ace2N-mNeon 5.7 ms.

photostabilityData.note: ASAP4b-Kv showed 32 ± 8% fluorescence loss (→ 68% remaining) after 60 s of continuous 100-mW/mm² one-photon illumination in hippocampal SST+ interneurons in vivo (powers 100–250 mW/mm² normalized to 100 mW/mm² assuming linearity).

twoPhoton.note: Under two-photon illumination ASAP3, ASAP4b and ASAP4e are all maximally excited at 938 nm (Ext. Fig. 3f); ASAP4b was used for extended two-photon in vivo recordings.

photobleach.note: In-vivo 1P photostability digitized from Fig. 2b (ASAP4b-Kv, cyan), hippocampal SST+ interneurons, continuous 453-nm widefield at 100 mW/mm² (acquired continuously at 400 fps for 60 s). Noisy in-vivo trace; t75≈59 s. Measured alongside ASAP3/ASAP4e (same figure → cross-overlay). NB the page's photostabilityData (68% at 1 min, Fig. 2b) is more pessimistic than this digitized trace (~0.78 at 60 s) — both kept.

Resonant-scanning TWO-PHOTON photobleaching of ASAP4b in cultured HEK293-Kir2.1 cells at 888 mW/mm² (right sub-panel of Ext. Fig. 4b; the left sub-panel is the same experiment at 518 mW/mm²). Digitized from the cyan trace, renormalized to its own first frame and overlay-verified. Fluorescence only falls to ~0.83 at the end of the 300-s window, so the 75% crossing is NEVER reached in-window: t75 is deliberately OMITTED (honest lower bound t75 > 300 s; the stretched-exponential fit would put it near 450 s, but nothing in the paper anchors an extrapolation that far). 2P entry, so no intensityMWmm2 and no 100-mW/mm² dose scaling. Same panel plots ASAP4e (~0.92), ASAP3 (~0.46) and the voltage-insensitive control ncpASAP4b (~0.20) → cross-overlay.

Galvanometric-scanning TWO-PHOTON photobleaching of ASAP4b in cultured HEK293-Kir2.1 cells at 960 mW/mm² over 5 min (Ext. Fig. 4c). Digitized from the blue trace, renormalized to its own first frame (0.96 on the plotted axis) and overlay-verified; only the continuous 0-5 min curve is stored, not the three post-dark recovery points at 6.7/8.3/10 min (the paper notes most of the 2P loss is reversible photoswitching, so this curve overstates true bleaching). Model-free t75 = 71 s from the digitized points; the stretched-exponential fit gives 69 s. 2P entry, so no intensityMWmm2 and no dose scaling. Same panel plots ASAP4e, ASAP3 and ncpASAP4b → cross-overlay. Under this harsher galvo scanning ASAP4b bleaches faster than ASAP3, the opposite of the resonant-scanning result in Ext. Fig. 4b.
